items.current:
It also checks the descriptor table:
only stdio and the broker-created FD3 socketpair end.
items.proposed:
It also checks the descriptor table while the child is still uid 0 in the
broker's domain: stdio, none of it a socket, and the two descriptors W4 places. These are the broker-created
socketpair end, which becomes FD3, and the verity-measured O_RDONLY worker script, which becomes fd 4. Every other
descriptor the child holds is closed in W4, before exec.
items.why: W3 checked that the child holds only stdio and the FD3 socketpair end. With fd 4 the worker's set is exactly {0..4}, and W3 checks it while the child is still uid 0 in the broker's domain, before W4 places the two descriptors and closes every other one (Q-HE5-9 (a), its post-exec half as re-ruled; the closed design, §3.2).

items.current:
The child runs broker-owned pre-exec code only:
close_range above 3, setresgid/setresuid to the signed UID, drop all
capabilities, `no_new_privs=1`, install the worker seccomp filter (W02d).
items.proposed:
The child runs broker-owned pre-exec code only, in raw system calls with no
allocation or lock: (1) block every signal, and reset every disposition except SIGKILL's and SIGSTOP's; (2) `dup3`
the socketpair end to 3 and the measured script descriptor to 4; (3) `close_range` from 5; (4) unblock;
(5) setresgid/setresuid to the signed UID; (6) drop all capabilities; (7) `no_new_privs=1`; (8) install the worker
seccomp filter (W02d).
items.why: W4's "close_range above 3" would close fd 4. The child now places the socketpair end at 3 and the measured script at 4 with dup3 and closes from 5, in raw system calls, with every signal blocked and every disposition but SIGKILL's and SIGSTOP's reset before, and unblocked after (the closed design, §3.2 and §3.5).

items.current:
W5. The child calls `execveat(fd, "", ..., AT_EMPTY_PATH)` on an O_PATH descriptor
of the fs-verity worker executable. The broker verified that descriptor's verity
digest before W2.
items.proposed:
W5. The child calls `execveat(4, "", ..., AT_EMPTY_PATH)` on fd 4, an O_RDONLY descriptor of the fs-verity worker
script, never O_PATH, because FS_IOC_MEASURE_VERITY needs a readable descriptor. The broker measured the verity
digest of that same open file description before W2, and never re-opens it. For a script, the kernel hands the
interpreter `/dev/fd/4`, which stays open in the worker and read-only: the verity file refuses every write open, and
the worker filter's openat admits read flags only (Q-HE5-9 (a)). After exec, the broker reads nothing of the
worker's `/proc` (owner decision Q-HE5-12 (b), "Drop post-exec reads"; SELinux matrix v6, XV1-7). The worker's
post-exec state holds by construction (O-R10-HE005) and is traced by
T04 (O-T04-HE5).
items.why: FS_IOC_MEASURE_VERITY needs a readable descriptor, so the exec descriptor is the measured O_RDONLY script, fd 4, one open file description from the measurement to the exec, never O_PATH and never re-opened; after exec the broker reads nothing of the worker's /proc (Q-HE5-9 (a); the owner's Q-HE5-12 (b), "Drop post-exec reads"; the closed design, §3.2 and §3.3).

## 14. Amendment HE5 (2026-10-26)

HE5 makes fd 4, the verity-checked O_RDONLY worker script, the one more descriptor the worker inherits beside FD3
(§5.4 W3-W5), and the broker reads nothing of the worker's `/proc` after exec. It is applied to the HS53 effective
text, which stays byte-identical; `architecture/host-interface-amendment-he5/amendment.json` gives every change and
its reason.

| Item | Where | Decisions |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | 5.4 W3, the descriptor check | Q-HE5-9, Q-EV12-1, MON-HE005-CLOSE |
| H2 | 5.4 W4, the child's pre-exec calls | Q-HE5-9, Q-EV12-1, MON-HE005-CLOSE |
| H3 | 5.4 W5, the exec descriptor | Q-HE5-9, Q-HE5-12, Q-EV12-1, MON-HE005-CLOSE |

Adopted text HE5 overrides (each file stays byte-identical; HE5 governs, and a successor of that contract adopts it):

| Superseded clause | In | Replaced by |
|---|---|---|
| "FD3 is the sole inherited non-stdio descriptor" | `docs/alpha-2/BROKER_HANDOFF_READINESS.md` | FD3 and fd 4 (the verity-checked, read-only worker script, Q-HE5-9 (a)) are the only inherited non-stdio descriptors (H1, H3) |
| "on an O_PATH descriptor of the worker executable" | `architecture/native-profile-v4/README.md` | on fd 4, an O_RDONLY descriptor of the verity-checked worker script (W01 §5.4 W5 as amended by HE5) (H3) |

Stated residuals:

- R-HE5-POSTEXEC: The worker's post-exec state is not observed at runtime: its descriptor set, credentials, capabilities, NoNewPrivs, filters and label. It holds by construction (the pinned child path, W3's observed pre-exec check, the kernel and the SELinux transition) and is traced by T04. This is the owner's Q-HE5-12 (b) choice: runtime detection on the host is given up, and T04 and HE-008's enrollment keep it. It is residual R1 of the closed HE-005 design (§8; MON-HE005-CLOSE). Follow-up: T04 and HE-008 (Q-HE5-12).

Edge record v12 registers the I02/I03 inputs beside this amendment (Q-EV12-1 (a)): R10's HE-005B vendors them
byte-identical, HE-005C and HE-005D implement W3-W5 as amended, and T04 confirms them on the enrolled kernel.

Obligations: O-R10-HE005 (W3-W5 as amended), O-T04-HE5 (native confirmation). Every E01-E12 obligation stays OPEN_UNPROVEN.
